fabs.name: Semiconductor Complex Limited (SCL)
fabs.operator: Ministry of Electronics & IT, Govt. of India
fabs.newsQuery: Semiconductor Complex Limited SCL Mohali India
fabs.brief: India's oldest operational semiconductor fab, run directly by the Ministry of Electronics & IT. Specializes in custom ASICs at 180nm for ISRO's satellite payloads and DRDO's defense systems. Not commercially oriented — its output goes almost entirely into India's strategic space and defense programs.

fabs.name: SPEL Semiconductor
fabs.brief: One of India's oldest private-sector semiconductor facilities, focused on outsourced assembly, testing, and packaging (OSAT) rather than wafer fabrication. Takes bare dies manufactured elsewhere and packages them into final chip form — a critical step in the semiconductor supply chain. Serves automotive and consumer electronics customers.

fabs.name: Micron Semiconductor ATP Facility
fabs.techNode: Assembly, Test & Packaging — DRAM & NAND Flash
fabs.newsQuery: Micron Technology semiconductor India Sanand Gujarat
fabs.brief: Micron's first semiconductor facility in India, focused on assembling, testing, and packaging DRAM and NAND flash memory chips — the kind found in smartphones, laptops, and servers. Micron is the world's third-largest memory chip maker. This facility won't fabricate silicon wafers but will handle the equally critical final stages of chip production.

fabs.name: Tata Electronics / PSMC Fab
fabs.newsQuery: Tata Electronics PSMC semiconductor fab Dholera India
fabs.brief: India's most ambitious true semiconductor fab — a wafer fabrication plant where silicon wafers are processed into chips. Tata has partnered with Taiwan's PSMC, which brings decades of foundry expertise. At 28nm, it targets the 'mature node' market: chips that are not cutting-edge but are in massive demand for automotive controllers, power management, and displays. Expected to be India's first large-scale commercial fab.

fabs.name: CG Power / Renesas Fab
fabs.operator: CG Power (India) + Renesas Electronics (Japan) + Stars Microelectronics (Thailand)
fabs.newsQuery: CG Power Renesas semiconductor fab India
fabs.brief: A tri-nation joint venture bringing together India's CG Power, Japan's Renesas (a leading automotive chip supplier), and Thailand's Stars Microelectronics. Will produce analog and power management chips — the workhorses of modern electronics that regulate voltage, manage batteries, and interface with the physical world. Analog chips at 40–90nm are less glamorous than cutting-edge logic, but they are irreplaceable in cars and industrial equipment.

fabs.name: Kaynes Semicon OSAT
fabs.brief: An outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) facility by Kaynes Technology, a leading Indian electronics manufacturer. Will specialize in high-reliability chip packaging for sectors where failure is not an option — automotive, medical, and aerospace. Advanced packaging technologies like system-in-package (SiP) can combine multiple chips into one compact, high-performance module.

fabs.name: ISMC Analog Fab
fabs.newsQuery: ISMC semiconductor fab India Karnataka Mysuru
fabs.brief: A proposed analog semiconductor fab that was originally backed by UAE-based Next Orbit Ventures in consortium with Tower Semiconductor (Israel). The project stalled after the primary investor withdrew and Intel's acquisition of Tower fell through. The Indian government is actively working to revive this project, as a 65nm analog fab would complement the logic fabs being built in Gujarat.

fabs.name: HCL – Foxconn OSAT
fabs.newsQuery: HCL Foxconn semiconductor OSAT India Jewar
fabs.brief: A joint venture between HCL and Foxconn (the world's largest electronics manufacturer) for semiconductor assembly and testing near the upcoming Noida International Airport. Foxconn brings deep experience in chip packaging from its operations in Asia. The proximity to a major air cargo hub is deliberate — chips are high-value, time-sensitive goods that move by air. An earlier, larger Foxconn-Vedanta deal collapsed in 2023 before this new arrangement was announced.
